problem: The stated necessary condition for perfect secrecy is incomplete. It names key length and uniformity but leaves out that the key must be independent of the message and used only once (the reuse point appears only later, in Section 2). Stated as a general theorem, students may read it as sufficient.
fix: Perfect secrecy needs at least as many keys as messages (for bit strings, a key as long as the message), the key uniformly random and independent of the message, and never reused. These conditions together are what the one-time pad meets.

problem: The answer stops at m₁ ⊕ m₂. In practice the XOR of two natural-language (or otherwise redundant) messages is enough to recover both plaintexts, so the answer understates what the attacker gains.
fix: c₁ ⊕ c₂ = 0011 = m₁ ⊕ m₂: the key is removed and the attacker learns the XOR of the two messages. When the messages are English text or other structured data, that XOR is usually enough to recover both plaintexts. The pad is never safe to reuse.
